title: ADR-002: Event Sourcing for Audit Log
content:
ADR-002: Event Sourcing for Audit Log

Status

Accepted

Context

The Auth Service handles sensitive operations: logins, logouts, token issuances, permission changes, and account lockouts. Compliance requirements (SOC2, GDPR) require a tamper-evident audit trail.

Options considered:

  1. Append-only SQL table — simplest, no ordering guarantees
  2. Event sourcing with Kafka — high operational overhead
  3. Event sourcing with Postgres WAL + logical decoding — complex setup
  4. Immutable event log table with ULID ordering — simple, correct, fast

Decision

Use an immutable append-only events table in Postgres with ULID primary keys. No events are ever updated or deleted. A separate process compresses old events into snapshots after 90 days.

This gives us:

  • Total ordering via ULID (time-sortable, monotonic)
  • Tamper evidence via sequential integrity checks
  • Simple query model (no projection needed for audit)
  • Zero operational overhead compared to Kafka

Consequences

Positive:

  • Simple to implement and audit
  • No additional infrastructure
  • Full history of every auth event forever (with 90-day compression)

Negative:

  • Not suitable for read-model projections at scale (not a problem for audit use)
  • Compression step must be carefully tested to avoid data loss
